row.evidence: Oracle Commerce internal user profiles are created by an administrator in User Management or via the Admin API (/ccadmin/v1/adminProfiles) and can only be deactivated, not deleted; SSO for internal users runs through Oracle Identity Cloud Service, and no SCIM endpoint is documented.
row.notes: New row. Quote-only product: Oracle publishes no Commerce base price (only an Additional Test Environment for Commerce Cloud Service add-on at $75,000/yr on the Fusion Cloud price list); oracle.com/cx/commerce and /ecommerce redirect to the generic CX page. No SCIM: none by absence after searching the Commerce REST API table of contents, the Using Oracle Commerce and Extending Oracle Commerce guides, the Okta OIN and the Entra gallery. Internal users can be managed through the Admin REST API (create, list, update incl. active flag and roles; no delete). SAML 2.0 or OIDC SSO for the admin and agent consoles is configured through Oracle Identity Cloud Service; new SSO users get dashboard access only until roles are added, which implies JIT creation.

plans.name: Oracle Commerce
plans.price_text: Contact Sales (no Commerce base price on Oracle's public price lists)
plans.notes: Only Commerce add-ons appear on the Fusion Cloud price list (Additional Test Environment for Commerce Cloud Service $75,000/yr).

scim.notes: No SCIM endpoint in the Oracle Commerce REST API table of contents or the Using/Extending Oracle Commerce guides. Internal users are created by an administrator in User Management or via the Admin API.

auth.notes: Registered application key (JWT) is exchanged at the login endpoint for a bearer access token.

limitations.text: Internal user profiles cannot be deleted, only deactivated; deactivation does not expire the password or secret key.

okta.notes: Okta OIN search for 'oracle' (2 pages) lists no Oracle Commerce app.

fallbacks.other_sync: SSO for internal users is brokered by Oracle Identity Cloud Service (OCI IAM identity domain) apps 'Oracle CX Commerce Admin' and 'Oracle CX Commerce Agent'
fallbacks.notes: JIT is implied, not stated: the SAML guide says users assigned in IDCS who sign in see only the dashboard until a Commerce administrator adds roles, because new users get dashboard access only.
